finding: The green 'straight only' at the west elm corner faces Rue Wellington arriving from the west (S158), not the split piece S187.
evidence: Mapillary signs 1082370960170279 and 710739533592883; both readings point to S158

finding: The 'left or right only' under the viaduct faces Rue Ann arriving from the north (S004).
evidence: Mapillary sign 1514662855914099; facing off by 1 degree, photos by 0 and 12 degrees

finding: In 2024 a 'straight only' under the viaduct faced Wellington S187. The city's post of October 2025 gives S187 a stop and 'left or right only'. No photo is newer than October 2025, so which one stands today needs a visit.
At the end of Brennan, bollards cross the street and no-entry signs stand at them. They close the paved area beyond to cars. The city file is right that cars may drive Brennan up to the bollards.
evidence: Mapillary sign 1442105399986997; photos show the bollards and paving continuing past them

finding: At the east end of Rue des Bassins, the no-entry sign hangs under a stop sign and faces the path into the new park. It closes the park to cars; Bassins itself stays two-way, as the city file says.
evidence: Mapillary sign 2817860535059873; faces the park connector within 2 degrees

finding: Two no-entry signs near the park path off Rue William. The photos show them at a lit crossing, but not which street they face.
evidence: Mapillary signs 2862599507242893 and 1238040140690599; readings 27 to 82 degrees off

finding: Rue de l'Inspecteur north of Notre-Dame is drawn by OpenStreetMap as two one-way halves, one towards Notre-Dame and one away. The no-entry sign guards the half coming towards Notre-Dame. The city draws one two-way line: coarser, not wrong.
evidence: Mapillary sign 1973817069759165 on the light pole at the corner; OSM ways 1353818496 (one-way towards Notre-Dame) and 457309753 (one-way away)
